item.title: Overgrown street trees obstructing parking, falling branches and bird fouling – Shawbury Road, 21st October
item.description:
Three street trees along Shawbury Road require attention, including two willow trees and a further tree towards the top of the road. The photographs show two of the affected trees. The branches have become overgrown and extend over the carriageway and parking spaces, making it difficult for vehicles to park close to the kerb without coming into contact with them. Drivers are consequently leaving large gaps between vehicles, reducing the available parking on a road that already suffers from a significant shortage of spaces. There is also a safety concern, as relatively large branches regularly fall during windy weather, posing a risk to pedestrians and parked vehicles. The willow tree approximately halfway down Shawbury Road also has a large bird’s nest, resulting in substantial amounts of bird droppings accumulating on parked vehicles, the pavement and the road. This is creating an ongoing cleanliness and hygiene issue. Please arrange for all three trees to be inspected and appropriately pruned, particularly the branches extending over parking spaces and the carriageway, and for any dead or potentially hazardous branches to be removed. I would also ask that the nest in the willow tree halfway down the road be inspected and, if inactive and legally permissible, removed as part of the pruning works to help prevent the bird-fouling problem recurring. The third tree towards the top of Shawbury Road should also be included in the inspection, although photographs of this tree are not currently available.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 16, Shawbury Road, East Dulwich, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
